item.text: {"candidates":[{"draft_id":"D0001","source_id":"MAC-010","claim":"Mexico's official debt statistics do not include the stock of T-bonds issued to the Bank of Mexico for liquidity management purposes, and the accounting practices adopted by the federal government and Banxico differ.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"adverse","actor":"Mexican federal government and Banxico","action":null,"mechanism":"accounting exclusion and divergent practices","outcome":"Incomplete and inconsistent public debt reporting","dates":[],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"The official debt statistics do not include the stock of T-bonds issued to the Bank of Mexico (Banxico) for liquidity management purposes, and the accounting practices adopted by the federal government and Banxico differ.","locator":"page 101","attribution":"IMF Staff Report, MAC-010, International Monetary Fund, 2022","period_fit":"Current period — as of the 2021/2022 review","source_limitations":["Source covers only reporting infrastructure, not actual policy outcomes or spending quality"],"question_ids":["5B.3","5B.7"],"verification_status":"pending","verification_notes":[],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0002","source_id":"MAC-010","claim":"Mexico reports 14 core and 9 encouraged Financial Soundness Indicators to the IMF monthly, but FSI reporting for the non-financial corporate sector is not reported, and reporting was temporarily interrupted after May 2021 pending IFRS9 migration.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"mixed","actor":"Mexican authorities","action":null,"mechanism":"voluntary FSI reporting to IMF; temporary suspension of publication","outcome":"Partial financial sector surveillance coverage; temporary interruption of published data","dates":["May 2021","expected resumption end of year following 2021"],"quantities":["14 core indicators","9 encouraged indicators","2 additional for OFCs","1 additional for households","1 additional for real estate markets"],"excerpt":"Mexico regularly reports monthly Financial Soundness Indicators (FSIs) to the IMF for publication. Currently, Mexico reports 14 core and 9 encouraged indicators for deposit takers, 2 additional FSI for OFCs,1 additional FSI for households and 1 additional FSI for real estate markets. FSIs on the non-financial corporate sector are not reported. Reporting has been temporarily interrupted following the publication of May 2021 data in order to revise historical and current data according to IFRS9 standards and is expected to resume by the end of the year.","locator":"page 101","attribution":"IMF Staff Report, MAC-010, International Monetary Fund, 2022","period_fit":"Current period — 2021/2022","source_limitations":["Only documents reporting practices, not actual financial sector soundness or policy quality"],"question_ids":["5B.7"],"verification_status":"pending","verification_notes":[],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0003","source_id":"MAC-010","claim":"Mexico's balance of payments and international investment position statistics migrated to the BPM6 sixth edition in 2017, but the External Debt Statistics Guide 2013 has not been fully implemented, with remaining issues including face-value recording of some financial institution liabilities and accrual-basis recording gaps for public sector external debt interest.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"adverse","actor":"Banxico","action":null,"mechanism":"incomplete international standard adoption","outcome":"External debt statistics missing intercompany external debt, SDR allocations; some liabilities at face rather than market value; public sector interest not on accrual basis","dates":["2017 migration to BPM6"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"In 2017, Banxico migrated the BOP and IIP statistics to the Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Manual (BPM6), sixth edition, with the publication of quarterly BPM6-based BOP data and IIP data . The External Debt Statistics, Guide for Compilers and Users, 2013 (EDS Guide) is yet to be fully implemented. Remaining issues relate to: (i) including the intercompany external debt and SDR allocations in external debt statistics disseminated by Banxico; (ii) extending the market valuation of liabilities to all financial institutions (some external debt are presented at face value); and (iii) recording the interest of the public sector external debt on an accrual basis.","locator":"page 101","attribution":"IMF Staff Report, MAC-010, International Monetary Fund, 2022","period_fit":"Current period — as of 2021/2022 review","source_limitations":["Documents statistical methodology gaps only; does not assess actual macroeconomic outcomes or policy quality"],"question_ids":["5B.3","5B.7"],"verification_status":"pending","verification_notes":[],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0004","source_id":"MAC-010","claim":"Mexico subscribed to the IMF's Special Data Dissemination Standard on August 13, 1996, and its latest SDDS Observance Report shows Mexico exceeds SDDS periodicity and timeliness requirements in many data categories while using flexibility options on central government debt and general government operations.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"favorable","actor":"Mexican government","action":null,"mechanism":"voluntary SDDS subscription and reporting","outcome":"Above-minimum transparency on many economic indicators; flexibility options used for debt and government operations reporting","dates":["August 13, 1996 (subscription date)","December 2021 (latest ROSC update)"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"Mexico subscribed to the IMF's Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS) on August 13, 1996. Mexico's latest SDDS Observance Report and metadata are available on the Dissemination Standards Bulletin Board. Mexico uses periodicity and timeliness flexibility options on central government debt and takes a timeliness flexibility option on general government operations. Mexico exceeds SDDS periodicity and timeliness requirements in many other data categories.","locator":"page 102","attribution":"IMF Staff Report, MAC-010, International Monetary Fund, 2022","period_fit":"Current period — 2021/2022 ROSC review","source_limitations":["Documents subscription status and self-reported compliance; flexibility options reduce comparability; does not assess actual policy quality"],"question_ids":["5B.7"],"verification_status":"pending","verification_notes":[],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0005","source_id":"MAC-010","claim":"Mexico reports monthly Financial Soundness Indicators to the IMF with full coverage of the Mexican financial system including gender-disaggregated financial access data, and participates in coordinated direct investment and portfolio investment surveys, disseminating reserve template and quarterly external debt statistics.","claim_type":"observed_fact","polarity":"favorable","actor":"Mexican authorities and Banxico","action":null,"mechanism":"regular FSI reporting; participation in coordinated international surveys; reserve template dissemination","outcome":"High coverage of financial system; gender-disaggregated financial access data; coordinated international investment position data","dates":[],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"Mexico regularly reports monthly Financial Soundness Indicators (FSIs) to the IMF for publication. Availability of data on other financial intermediaries such as insurance companies and pension funds allow for the construction of a financial corporation's survey with full coverage of the Mexican financial system. Mexico reports data on some indicators of the Financial Access Survey (FAS), including gender disaggregated data on the use of basic financial services and the two indicators (commercial bank branches per 100,000 adults and ATMs per 100,000 adults) adopted by the UN to monitor Target 8.10 of the Sustainable Development Goals. The authorities participate in the coordinated direct investment survey and coordinated portfolio investment survey and disseminate the data template on international reserves and foreign currency liquidity (reserve template) and quarterly external debt statistics.","locator":"page 101","attribution":"IMF Staff Report, MAC-010, International Monetary Fund, 2022","period_fit":"Current period — 2021/2022","source_limitations":["Reports only on data availability and coverage, not on actual financial sector health or policy quality"],"question_ids":["5B.7"],"verification_status":"pending","verification_notes":[],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0006","source_id":"MAC-010","claim":"IMF data ROSC 2021 assessment found Mexico's monetary statistics methodological foundations generally sound, and ESS (external sector statistics) are of high quality, with the IIP and external debt consistency rated largely observed to observed, and national accounts consistency rated largely observed to observed for most categories.","claim_type":"source_assertion","polarity":"favorable","actor":"IMF ROSC assessment (2021)","action":null,"mechanism":"IMF ROSC methodology applied in July 2021","outcome":"Generally sound monetary statistics methodology; high-quality external sector statistics; largely observed to observed ratings for consistency between IIP and external debt","dates":["ROSC conducted July 2021","published December 2021"],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"The methodological foundations of monetary statistics are generally sound. The 2021 data ROSC update found that ESS are of a high quality.","locator":"page 101","attribution":"IMF Staff Report, MAC-010, International Monetary Fund, 2022","period_fit":"Current period — 2021 ROSC assessment","source_limitations":["Self-assessment subject to IMF methodological standards; ROSC reflects institutional framework rather than actual policy outcomes; ROSC conducted July 2021"],"question_ids":["5B.7"],"verification_status":"pending","verification_notes":[],"premium_verification_required":false},{"draft_id":"D0007","source_id":"MAC-010","claim":"The IMF recommended that Mexico publish a consolidated table of all institutional units in the public sector with unified accounting standards at the sub-national level, which would improve measurement of public fixed investment in national accounts.","claim_type":"recommendation","polarity":"context","actor":"IMF","action":null,"mechanism":"formal IMF recommendation in Staff Report","outcome":"Recommendation for improved public sector accounting transparency and sub-national accounting standardization","dates":[],"quantities":[],"excerpt":"It recommended publishing a table of all institutional units in the public sector and its subsectors, clearly grouping them according to: 1) the coverage of units used in the national presentation; 2) the coverage used in the international presentation; and 3) the subsectors of the public sector as described in the GFSM2014. A full adoption of uniform accounting standards at the sub-national level would help obtain an improved measure of public fixed investment in the national accounts.","locator":"page 101","attribution":"IMF Staff Report, MAC-010, International Monetary Fund, 2022","period_fit":"Current period — 2021/2022 review","source_limitations":["This is an unfulfilled recommendation, not an observed fact about actual policy execution"],"question_ids":["5B.3","5B.7"],"verification_status":"pending","verification_notes":[],"premium_verification_required":false}],"inspected_locator_count":4,"locator_dispositions":[{"locator":"page 101","disposition":"evidence_extracted","explanation":"Content describes Mexico's statistical infrastructure: public sector accounting gaps, monetary/financial statistics methodology, FSI reporting practices, BPM6 migration status, external sector statistics quality, and an IMF recommendation for improved accounting standards. Relevant to 5B.3 (fiscal/monetary rules), 5B.7 (reliable information/audit), and indirectly to economic trajectory assessment."},{"locator":"page 102","disposition":"evidence_extracted","explanation":"Content documents Mexico's SDDS subscription (since 1996), latest ROSC update (December 2021), and use of flexibility options on central government debt and general government operations. Relevant to 5B.7 (transparency/reliable information/publication of economic data)."},{"locator":"page 103","disposition":"evidence_extracted","explanation":"Table of Common Indicators shows reporting frequency and data quality assessments. Revenue, expenditure, balance, and composition of financing data rated LO (largely observed) to O (observed) for accuracy; reliability rated O across categories. Relevant to 5B.7 (reliable information/independent audit/evaluation)."},{"locator":"page 104","disposition":"evidence_extracted","explanation":"Continuation of Common Indicators table. External Current Account Balance, Gross External Debt, and International Investment Position all rated LO to O for accuracy and O for reliability. Consumer Price Index rated O, O, LNO, O for accuracy and LO, LNO, O, O, O for reliability (some largely not observed rating). Relevant to 5B.7."}],"material_omissions":[],"unresolved_gaps":[{"question_ids":["5B.1","5B.2","5B.4","5B.5","5B.6","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10"],"gap":"This IMF Staff Report covers data standards and statistical infrastructure quality (ROS C), not actual economic policy substance. No evidence is present on: legislative agenda for prosperity (5B.1), appointments of economic professionals (5B.2), competition/anti-corruption enforcement against politically connected actors (5B.5), actual infrastructure/education/health/administrative capacity outcomes from budgets (5B.6), tax/labor/wage policy incidence across classes and regions (5B.8), or shock response measures (5B.9), or net economic trajectory assessment (5B.10). These questions require different source types (policy documents, procurement records, program evaluations, household surveys, or macroeconomic outcome data)."}]}
